newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman asks House to remove CRP cap.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman asks House to remove CRP cap.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman on Thursday urged the U.S. House appropriations committee to reconsider its vote to limit new enrollment in the agency's Conservation Reserve Program.

"I hope you reconsider the amendment to ensure that USDA has the maximum flexibility" to meet its goal of signing up 14 million acres for the program this year, Glickman said in a letter addressed to New York Rep. James Walsh.

The House committee voted earlier Thursday to cap new farm enrollment in the CRP at 14 million acres. The USDA had planned to enroll some 19 million acres in the program that pays rental fees to farmers to take environmentally sensitive land out of production.
Walsh, a Republican, said that most of the benefits of the CRP program went to Midwest farmers and it was time to give other geographic areas more of the benefits.
The item was part of an emergency spending bill to help U.S. flood victims, and the bill may be debated by the full House as early as next week.

The 14 million acre ceiling would mean the loss of environmental benefits from acreage currently enrolled in the CRP with practices designed to help water quality, soil erosion and wildlife, Glickman said.
In his letter, Glickman said USDA was limited by law to paying rental rates for the CRP based on local market values.

But the agency is "considering whether higher incentive payments" can be made to attract offers for the highest priority land, he said. "This may provide a more viable option to use CRP in areas of high land use competition pressures," he said.
